matches.rationale: Both identify the same issue: the Abstract claims TTFT reduction of 4.2× and throughput of 3.2–4.5×, but these figures do not align with the experimental results in Figures 5 and 6. Finding 1 documents the cross-section inconsistency between Abstract and results sections, matching the ground truth's evidence manipulation claim.

Ground truth 2 concerns a logical inconsistency in Section 3.1 where burst tolerance is defined inconsistently (ratio vs. difference). No finding addresses this method logic issue in the burst tolerance definition or Equation 1.

Ground truth 3 identifies missing baseline configuration details (batch sizes, KV cache settings, chunked prefill) in Section 4.1. No finding addresses this experimental protocol omission regarding baseline system configuration.

Ground truth 4 identifies that the text claims 4.5× and 3.2× throughput gains on ShareGPT-4o, but Figure 6 shows lower values (closer to 3.1× and 2.8×). Finding 1 captures this same Abstract-vs-Results mismatch for throughput metrics.

Ground truth 5 concerns an unsupported generalization claim about 'universal applicability across all MLLM architectures' when only two models were tested. No finding addresses this overgeneralization in Section 4.2.
Ground truth 6 identifies fabrication of a non-existent reference [61] (Zhang et al.) in Section 5 Related Work. No finding addresses this fabricated citation issue.

Ground truth 7 concerns logical inconsistency between Equations 2 and 3 in Section 3.2, where different penalty factors (w vs. β) and cost structures are used without explanation. No finding addresses this equation inconsistency.

Ground truth 8 identifies missing ethical considerations and data provenance information for the VisualWebInstruct and ShareGPT-4o datasets in Section 4.1. No finding addresses this ethical integrity omission.
Ground truth 9 concerns promotional language in the Introduction claiming ElasticMM 'completely eliminates all inference bottlenecks.' No finding addresses this rhetorical overstatement.

Ground truth 10 identifies that the Abstract lists 'unified multimodal prefix caching' as part of elastic partition scheduling, but Section 3.2 does not mention it in that context. No finding addresses this narrative misalignment.

Ground truth 11 concerns Section 4.3 claiming both optimizations provide 'roughly equal' gains when Figure 8 likely shows unequal contributions. No finding addresses this ablation study misrepresentation.

Ground truth 12 identifies an unfair comparison where ElasticMM allegedly uses 'optimized CUDA kernels and custom memory allocators not available to baselines.' No finding addresses this experimental protocol issue.

Ground truth 13 concerns the Conclusion claiming ElasticMM 'guarantees SLO compliance under all workload conditions' when results show conditional compliance. No finding addresses this overgeneralization in the Conclusion.

Ground truth 14 identifies misattribution of encoder-decoder MLLM architectures to Vaswani et al. [10]. Finding 2 identifies a different but related misattribution: LLaMA-3.2 Vision cited to reference [21] (Llama Guard 3 Vision) instead of the correct base model. Both are reference fabrication/misattribution issues, though at different locations.
Ground truth 15 identifies missing discussion of limitations and societal impacts in the Conclusion. No finding addresses this ethical integrity omission regarding limitations or negative impacts.
